frequency_question: How often does the central bank implement extraordinary liquidity measures like iCRR or special windows when banking system liquidity surges beyond target parameters?
membership_rule: Includes any formal RBI circular, press release, or monetary policy statement introducing an incremental cash reserve ratio or equivalent temporary high-powered reserve constraint since 2004. Excludes standard bi-monthly repo rate adjustments or standard CRR changes.

cases.name: Incremental CRR (iCRR) on FCNR(B) and 2023 Bond Inflows

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named exact instances of extraordinary quantity-based reserve tightening instruments deployed in response to sudden liquidity gluts over 22 years.
known_gaps: Minor ad-hoc variable repo rate (VRR) auctions are excluded as they are standard operations rather than structural incremental reserve mandates.
skeleton: RBI monetary policy cycles characterized by extreme systemic liquidity surpluses requiring non-standard quantity-based absorption instruments.
multiplier: 3 verified historical interventions across 3 major systemic liquidity surplus episodes spanning 22 years.
validity_reason: Central bank statutory powers under the RBI Act remain unchanged and institutional appetite for deploying targeted liquidity tools persists across governor tenures.
